pull_requests.title: [Spec] DFlash2: local convolution + candidate selector
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

Two additions to the DFlash draft, both switched on by the checkpoint. A DFlash
checkpoint declares neither and takes the path it always took.

**Grouped dynamic depthwise convolution** inside each block, so a proposal
position can see the ones before it without another backbone pass.
`out[i,c] = Σ_t (base[t,c] + δ[i,t,g(c)]) · x[i−t,c]`, taps zero across the block
boundary. Wraps each sublayer in and out from one projection of its input.
On when `conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` are set.

**Candidate selector.** Instead of an independent argmax per slot, keep the
target head's top-K per slot, score adjacent transitions
`edge(p→c) = ⟨A[p] ⊙ project(h), B[c]⟩ + unary[c]`, and walk the best path from
the verified anchor. At T>0 it walks by inverse CDF and returns q over the K
candidates for the lossless verify. On when `selector_rank` and
`selector_top_k` are set.

## Modifications

```
srt/models/dflash.py                 the convolution, the selector, the walk kernel
srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py      four config fields
srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py  the proposal and the T>0 verify
```

The selector's decode is folded into the draft CUDA graph, greedy and sampled
alike. The walk is one Triton program per request: a slot's K scores stay in
registers, greedy rows take the argmax and emit a one-hot q, and the slot-to-slot
dependency is a loop inside the program rather than a kernel per slot. No new
server args, no new env vars, nothing outside DFlash touched.

## Accuracy Tests

```
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_logits.py
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_spec_aux_hidden_state.py
```

`4 passed` and `5 passed`. `test_dflash_logits.py` covers the selector's sampled path end to end,
the mixed greedy/sampling batch — each row identical to running it alone, with
greedy rows asserted to carry a one-hot q — and the rejection of a quantized
target LM head.

Lossless decoding is the property that matters here and it is structural: greedy
walks emit the point mass at the token they take, and sampled walks return the
realized q over the K candidates, so the verify sees the proposal distribution it
actually drew from.

## Speed Tests and Profiling


Published evaluation for
[`z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2)
on `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`: SGLang on one H200 with FlashAttention 3, block size 8
(seven draft tokens per verification step), Qwen3.8's recommended sampling
(temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20) at `xhigh` reasoning effort, 4096 max new
tokens, prompts formatted by [`z-lab/dflash`](https://github.com/z-lab/dflash).
Compared against the target's built-in MTP and a community DSpark drafter,
[`RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-DSpark),
both also proposing seven tokens per step.

### Acceptance length

Per-request mean of completion tokens over verification steps.

| Dataset | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 |
|---------|----:|-------:|---------:|
| GSM8K | 5.02 | 4.36 | **5.46** |
| MATH-500 | 4.72 | 3.92 | **5.28** |
| HumanEval | 3.91 | 3.30 | **4.39** |
| MBPP | 3.99 | 3.51 | **4.79** |
| MT-Bench | 3.74 | 3.01 | **4.10** |

### Throughput, GSM8K

Output tokens over end-to-end wall time, with speedup over autoregressive
decoding.

| conc | autoregressive | MTP | DSpark | DFlash 2 |
|------|---------------:|----:|-------:|---------:|
| 1 | 68.9 | 178.5 (2.59×) | 185.3 (2.69×) | **236.1 (3.43×)** |
| 8 | 467.2 | 1,022.1 (2.19×) | 1,040.8 (2.23×) | **1,328.7 (2.84×)** |
| 32 | 1,329.8 | 1,381.1 (1.04×) | 1,506.5 (1.13×) | **1,922.5 (1.45×)** |

Full tables for the other four datasets, and for
[`z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/z-lab/Muse-Glimmer-30B-DFlash2)
against Meta's published DFlash assistant, are on the model cards.

### What it costs

The convolution and the selector are the whole difference between a DFlash draft
and a DFlash 2 draft, so their cost is what a step loses by having them. Measured
against Meta's published DFlash assistant on the same target,
[`meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B`](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B),
block 16, GSM8K, four H200 shards. `cost` is `(1 + accept gain) / (1 + throughput
gain) - 1` — the throughput gain the extra acceptance would have produced had the
step stayed the same length, against the gain it actually produced.

| conc | acceptance | throughput | cost | | acceptance | throughput | cost |
|------|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|---|-----------:|-----------:|-----:|
| | **T=0** | | | | **T=1** | | |
| 1 | +13.6% | +11.7% | 1.7% | | +24.4% | +21.1% | 2.7% |
| 8 | +14.0% | +11.4% | 2.3% | | +24.5% | +21.5% | 2.5% |
| 32 | +14.1% | +11.9% | 2.0% | | +24.0% | +21.2% | 2.3% |
| 64 | +14.0% | +12.3% | 1.5% | | +24.3% | +22.2% | 1.7% |

So 1.5–2.7%, and it falls as the batch grows: the target verify grows with the
batch while the selector's work does not keep pace. It falls as the target grows
for the same reason.

Acceptance enters this table only as a ratio between the two drafts, both
measured the same way — as total accepted tokens over total verification steps,
where the model card reports a mean over per-request ratios. The two statistics
differ on absolute values but nearly cancel in the gain: +24.3% here at
concurrency 64 against the card's +21.0% for the same pair of checkpoints.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

pull_requests.title: feat: add optimized Domino rollout to DFlash V2
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

This PR adds optimized Domino projector support to DFlash V2 for the public
`Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16` checkpoint. It is based on the latest upstream
`main` and supersedes the earlier Domino PRs #31328 and #36860.

The target verification, continuous-prefix acceptance, bonus-token handling,
and KV-cache commit paths remain unchanged.

## Included implementation

- Parse, validate, instantiate, and load the bias-free prefix GRU and the
  two-layer SiLU correction projector.
- Generate the 15-token Domino proposal chain for block size 16, feeding each
  realized proposal back into the GRU.
- Precompute all base LM-head logits in one step-major projection.
- Capture the complete rollout in the DFlash draft CUDA Graph, with eager
  fallback when graphs are unavailable.
- Use ATen `GRUCell` for one-token feedback updates to avoid repeated cuDNN
  weight packing.
- Add a request-local, block-shared K=2048 candidate vocabulary pool for the
  correction head. `K=0` remains the full-vocabulary reference path.

## Scope

- BF16, CUDA, TP=1, Qwen3-8B, DFlash block size 16.
- Greedy decoding path; target verification remains full-vocabulary and is the
  correctness boundary.
- The candidate pool is a draft-side approximation; it does not alter target
  verification semantics.
- Non-greedy sampling and tensor-parallel Domino are covered by follow-up work
  in PR #37069.

## Validation

### Unit and registered tests

Focused tests:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_dflash_domino.py

CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 PYTHONPATH=python3 -m pytest -q -s \
  test/registered/spec/dflash/test_dflash_domino.py
```

The focused suite covers config parsing, strict Domino projector weight loading,
shape validation, full-chain rollout parity, candidate-pool boundaries,
batched-vs-single-row parity, eager fallback, and CUDA Graph replay.

### Serving validation setting

We validated the Qwen3-8B DFlash/Domino serving path with the following fixed setting:

- Target: `Qwen/Qwen3-8B`
- Drafts: `Qwen3-8B-DFlash-b16` and `Qwen3-8B-Domino-b16`
- CUDA, BF16, TP=1, FA3 attention backend
- DFlash block size: 16 (15 proposed tokens)
- Domino candidate pool: K=2048
- Greedy sampling: `temperature=0`, `top_p=1`, `top_k=1`
- Qwen3 tokenizer chat template, thinking disabled
- Workloads: GSM8K-128, HumanEval-164, MT-Bench-80
- Concurrency: 1, 8, 32; maximum generation length: 2048
- Server: `max_running_requests=32`, `cuda_graph_max_bs=32`,
  `mem_fraction_static=0.70`, `page_size=1`
- Warmup: 3 requests, warmup maximum generation 1024, first request skipped
- One measured run per configuration, timeout 3600 seconds

The serving validation completed successfully for both DFlash and Domino on this setting.
Numerical throughput and acceptance-length comparisons are reported separately in PR #37069.

## Changes

This branch is rebased directly onto the current upstream `main`; no unrelated
benchmark or training scripts are included.

Extend the optimized Domino rollout from PR #36899 to tensor parallel (TP>1), including CUDA Graph capture and eager fallback paths.

- Compute first-token argmax from vocab-sharded LM-head logits with deterministic global tie handling.
- Add a full-vocabulary TP gather path for small logical tensors.
- Add a compact global candidate-pool path for larger batches/graphs: local top-k, TP all-gather, and candidate base-logit all-reduce.
- Validate LM-head and embedding shard metadata, padded vocab layout, TP rank, and unsupported added-vocab layouts.
- Keep B=1 on full gather and use compact candidate pooling for B>1 CUDA-graph buckets.

- SGLang nightly DLC unit test: `29 passed, 35 subtests passed`.

pull_requests.title: [Spec] Add LiLiCorr: a candidate-lattice reranker for DFlash drafts
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

DFlash is trained on per-position marginals rather than on the joint block distribution, so its
drafted tokens are individually plausible yet **jointly incoherent** — slot 3 may be a fine
continuation of the prompt while contradicting the token DFlash itself chose for slot 2.

**LiLiCorr** keeps the top-`k` candidates DFlash already produces at each block position and scores
_transitions_ between adjacent candidates with a small two-layer transformer, then commits a path
through the resulting lattice greedily, left to right, instead of taking the per-slot argmax. One
network pass produces every vector, the pairwise scores are a single batched matmul, and only the
greedy walk stays sequential. **Verify is untouched, so outputs remain distributionally identical to**
**the target model's** — only acceptance length and throughput change.

* Paper: LiLiCorr: Lightweight Likelihood Correlation of Parallel Drafts for Speculative Decoding (arXiv:2608.20530)
* Blog: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/nemotron/lilicorr/
* **Companion PR — training:** NVIDIA/Model-Optimizer#2342

This PR is the **serving** half. It ships no checkpoints and no training code; the companion PR
above trains the drafters and exports them in the format this loader reads.

## Performance

**How these were produced.** Six drafters for a **Qwen3-8B** target, all trained in **NVIDIA**
**ModelOpt** on one matched contract — the same corpus, schedule and block geometry for every arm, so
no row carries a training advantage. Training data is NVIDIA's Nemotron Post-Training Dataset v2
with the multilingual split excluded, generated from the target with **thinking disabled**;
**6 epochs**; block size 16 (15 drafted slots, 16 verified); DFlash decay objective at gamma 7;
**8 nodes × 8 H100, global batch size 64** (one sequence per device, no gradient accumulation).

All six were then exported and **served through the code in this PR** on a **single H100 80GB**,
`tp_size 1`, at concurrency 1, greedy `T=0`, `--attention-backend fa3`, `draft_length 15`, mean of
two replicates, with the **whole node held exclusive per benchmark** so nothing else shared it.
Speedup is output tokens/s against an autoregressive baseline measured **in the same allocation**,
because a denominator borrowed from another node carries that node's clock into every ratio.

Three of the five alternatives — `DFlash`, `DSpark`, `Domino` — already live in this repo.

Cells are `acceptance length / speedup-vs-AR`; **★ fastest, ☆ second fastest**:

| benchmark       | LiLiCorr+conv   | LiLiCorr        | DSpark        | DFlash2         | Domino        | DFlash        |
| --------------- | --------------- | --------------- | ------------- | --------------- | ------------- | ------------- |
| gsm8k           | ★ 7.715 / 5.26x | ☆ 7.557 / 5.22x | 7.375 / 4.86x | 7.252 / 5.06x   | 7.225 / 4.87x | 6.341 / 4.59x |
| math500         | ★ 9.241 / 6.54x | ☆ 9.064 / 6.52x | 9.012 / 6.15x | 8.999 / 6.49x   | 8.976 / 6.25x | 7.909 / 5.88x |
| aime25          | ★ 8.285 / 6.03x | ☆ 8.156 / 6.03x | 8.043 / 5.61x | 7.967 / 5.91x   | 8.066 / 5.77x | 7.126 / 5.44x |
| humaneval       | ★ 7.393 / 4.01x | 7.077 / 3.93x   | 7.163 / 3.72x | ☆ 7.081 / 3.95x | 6.864 / 3.73x | 6.156 / 3.68x |
| mbpp\_sanitized | ★ 5.999 / 4.18x | ☆ 5.849 / 4.13x | 5.888 / 3.95x | 5.685 / 4.05x   | 5.679 / 3.91x | 5.027 / 3.70x |
| livecodebench   | ★ 7.975 / 5.40x | ☆ 7.754 / 5.33x | 7.775 / 5.10x | 7.601 / 5.26x   | 7.553 / 5.04x | 6.808 / 4.88x |
| alpaca\_eval    | ☆ 3.697 / 2.69x | ★ 3.656 / 2.70x | 3.588 / 2.52x | 3.467 / 2.58x   | 3.627 / 2.59x | 3.222 / 2.46x |
| mtbench         | ★ 4.014 / 2.94x | ☆ 3.939 / 2.93x | 3.957 / 2.78x | 3.748 / 2.80x   | 3.948 / 2.84x | 3.478 / 2.67x |

**Against every other approach in the table, LiLiCorr with convolutions is the fastest on all eight**
**benchmarks.** Plain LiLiCorr is the fastest on seven of the eight; the exception is humaneval, a
164-prompt slice, where DFlash2 is ahead by 0.5%.

`DFlash` is the deliberately head-free control. Against it, the reranked drafter is worth
**+9.1% to +14.6% output tokens/s** — the number to read if the question is "what does this buy over
what I already run":

| benchmark                      | gsm8k      | mbpp\_sanitized | math500    | livecodebench | mtbench   | humaneval |
| ------------------------------ | ---------- | --------------- | ---------- | ------------- | --------- | --------- |
| throughput vs head-free DFlash | **+14.6%** | **+12.9%**      | **+11.1%** | **+10.5%**    | **+9.9%** | **+9.1%** |

Every head also clears that control by **+7.60% to +21.67%** on acceptance, on every arm and every
benchmark, which is the check that a head actually loaded rather than silently falling back.

**Acceptance length is bit-reproducible under greedy decoding; throughput is not.** The replicate
spread on acceptance was 0.00% on every benchmark; on throughput it is about 0.2% within one
allocation, and about 1% across allocations.

ⓘ **Reproducing these needs `--attention-backend fa3`.** Backends that publish `seq_lens_cpu` every
step pay a device-to-host sync per block, worth about 8% here. That is a property of DFlash decoding
rather than of LiLiCorr, and the new docs subsection explains which backends are affected and why.
Backends also differ in attention numerics, so acceptance measured on different backends does not
belong in one table.

## Modifications

**No new `SpeculativeAlgorithm`, no worker subclass, no registration, no CLI flag, and no new**
**entry in any choices list.** Two environment variables gate the opt-in sampled commit described
below; nothing else reads the environment. LiLiCorr rides `--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` and is
selected by the checkpoint declaring `architectures: ["LiLiCorrDraftModel"]`, exactly as
`DFlash2DraftModel` selects the candidate selector. If you go looking for the registration, that is
why there isn't one.

10 files, **+3,076 / −1**. The single deleted line is one `if` in the draft loop that gained a
branch; everything else is an addition.

**Only four files already existed — +164 / −1 between them:**

| file                                              | added        | what                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| srt/speculative/dflash\_worker\_v2.py             | **+95 / −1** | five dispatch seams: two `__init__` assignments, the fold branch in `_maybe_build_draft_sampler`, the guarded anchor publication inside `_append_target_hidden_to_draft_kv_by_loc`, and a fourth arm on the existing three-way draft-loop branch |
| srt/models/dflash.py                              | **+2**       | `DFlashDraftModel` declares `lilicorr: Optional[nn.Module] = None` beside the existing `candidate_selector`, and stores the `rms_norm_eps` it already computes                                                     |
| docs/.../speculative\_decoding.mdx                | +34          | two subsections under "DFlash Decoding"                                                                                                                                                                           |
| test/registered/unit/spec/test\_dflash\_logits.py | +33          | one worker-stub test: the sampled arm's device gate                                                                                                                                                               |

For scale, `selector` (DFlash2 — the closest precedent, also a head on the same draft model, also
checkpoint-selected) appears on 43 lines of that worker; `lilicorr` appears on 30.

**New, self-contained:**

* `srt/models/lilicorr.py` (632) — the head, `LiLiCorrDraftModel(DFlashDraftModel)`, `EntryClass`, and the two weight-coverage checks
* `kernels/ops/speculative/lilicorr.py` (520) — three Triton kernels; see "Why the custom kernels" below
* `srt/speculative/lilicorr_utils.py` (656) — head geometry, the candidate lattice, the eager draft seam and the CUDA-graph-folded draft sampler, in one module beside `dflash_utils.py`
* `test/registered/unit/spec/test_lilicorr.py` (805) — 46 CPU tests
* `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_lilicorr_cuda.py` (216) — 18 GPU tests pinning the Triton kernels against their torch references
* `test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_dflash_lilicorr.py` (84) — the E2E server test, registered `disabled=` until a drafter is published

## The head runs inside the draft CUDA graph, and that is the whole optimization

The head is a long tail of small kernels, so what it costs is **host dispatch**, not FLOPs. It
therefore rides the seam DFlash already has for exactly this: `_maybe_build_draft_sampler` runs
before `init_cuda_graphs`, and the sampler is registered on
`draft_model_runner.capture_tail_hooks` through `make_draft_sampler_capture_hook` — the same
mechanism DFlash2's `_SelectorDraftSampler` and DSpark's `DsparkDraftSampler` use, and
`LiLiCorrDraftSampler` has the same shape as the latter: static buffers sized from the capture
buckets, host-side staging of the per-row sampling params before the replay, an in-graph philox
draw, and the drafted tokens written into a static `out` the worker reads after the replay.

Nothing in the head is capture-hostile: static shapes, no collectives at `tp=1`, no host syncs, a
fixed decode trip count, and every parameter-derived buffer built by
`materialize_inference_buffers` before capture.

**There is no `torch.compile` anywhere in this PR.** An earlier revision compiled the captured
body, on the theory that the graph removes the launches' host cost while leaving their number and
memory traffic alone. Measured end to end on one H100 — Qwen3-8B, gsm8k, greedy, `fa3`, `tp_size 1`,
both arms as sequential cells in **one allocation** so the node term cancels — it is a null:

| requests | concurrency | compiled | no compile | Δ acceptance | Δ output tok/s |
| -------: | ----------: | -------- | ---------- | -----------: | -------------: |
| 1319     | 1           | 6.9951 / 731.5 | 6.9947 / 735.6 | −0.005% | +0.56% |
| 1319     | 1           | 6.9951 / 739.7 | 6.9947 / 735.0 | −0.005% | −0.62% |
| 1319     | 32          | 7.0085 / 10179.5 | 7.0022 / 10131.9 | −0.090% | −0.47% |
| 320      | 32          | 7.0650 / 9410.8 | 7.0576 / 9489.0 | −0.105% | +0.83% |

Four pairs straddling zero, against a 1.12% spread for the *same* arm measured in two different
allocations. The fold, by contrast, is load-bearing: in the same allocation and on the same tree,
forcing the head out of the graph with `SGLANG_DFLASH_EAGER_DRAFT_SAMPLER=1` costs **−8.4%**.

So there is no dynamo surface here at all — no compile prewarm, no recompile-limit handling, no
`torch._inductor.config` mutation. The one operational note that remains is that the head should run
on the folded path: an eager fallback exists for the steps the graph cannot serve and is correct but
costs a large fraction of throughput, and because acceptance is identical either way that shows up
only in tokens/s. `build_lilicorr_draft_sampler` warns with a reason when it declines to fold, and
the worker warns once if a decode step lands on the eager head.

Two capture gaps remain, both shared with the existing DFlash heads. Prefill and extend run eager —
the eager seam is the third arm of the same `elif` chain that already carries the selector's and
plain DFlash's. And `tp>1` declines to fold, because the candidate top-k needs a packed all-gather
inside the graph.

## Convolutional drafters are supported, and the support is a refusal

The leading column of the table above is LiLiCorr composed with the grouped dynamic convolutions
that wrap each DFlash sublayer. It serves through this PR, and that is worth stating precisely,
because it is **not** a feature this PR adds.

The convolution belongs to the **DFlash backbone**, not to the reranker: `LiLiCorrDraftModel`
extends `DFlashDraftModel` and therefore inherits the `__init__` that builds it from
`conv_kernel_size` and `conv_group_size` in `dflash_config`. Both the plain and the convolutional
drafter already load and run through the same path, with no new flag and no new code.

What this PR contributes is the **refusal**. Both geometry keys default to `0`, so a checkpoint whose
config lost them builds no convolution modules at all — and the backbone loader then drops every
convolution tensor it cannot resolve. That is correct behaviour for rotary caches and the worst
possible behaviour here: all 20 tensors of a five-layer drafter disappear in silence, the draft
serves as its convolution-free parent, and the only symptom is an acceptance length that is lower
than it should be and entirely believable. `check_conv_weight_coverage` refuses any checkpoint whose
convolution tensors and built modules disagree, in either direction. Five of the CPU tests cover it:
the matched case, the convolution-free case, both silent-drop directions, and a partial checkpoint.

## Sampling the committed path (opt-in)

At `T > 0` the target samples, but the head committed the per-slot argmax and verify was handed a
point mass, so each slot was paid `p(argmax)` rather than the overlap of the two distributions.
`LILICORR_SAMPLING=1` draws each slot from `softmax(scores / T)` over that slot's candidates, at the
request's own temperature, and publishes the proposal it drew from into the same buffers the DFlash2
selector already fills — so the accept path is untouched and verify stays exact. Greedy requests
sharing the batch take the argmax and report a one-hot proposal. On Qwen3-8B it is worth about 6%
acceptance and 6% end-to-end at `T = 1`, at under 1% of the per-block wall.

Off by default, and with it unset the captured body is `select` itself rather than something
equivalent to it, so `T = 0` output is unchanged bit for bit.
`SGLANG_LILICORR_REQUIRE_SAMPLING=1` refuses to start if the mode was asked for but is not enabled.
Both are read once at import: the sampler is replayed from a captured draft graph, so a per-call
read would be a host-side branch inside a replay — happy to move them to `ServerArgs` fields
resolved at init if you would rather.

The sampled commit is additionally gated on the same supported-device condition as the selector's,
on both the folded and the eager path, because it publishes into an accept kernel that does not run
everywhere. Where it is unsupported the arm falls back to the argmax commit and the existing verify.

## Why the custom kernels

`kernels/ops/speculative/lilicorr.py` is the single largest new file after the head itself, so it is
worth saying up front what it buys. All three kernels dispatch to a value-identical torch
implementation off CUDA, which is also what makes the head exercisable in a CPU unit test.

**`lilicorr_topk_lse` — exact per-row top-k _and_ the full-vocab log-partition from one pass over**
**`[n, V]`.** The head scores log-probs normalized over the whole vocabulary, so it needs the partition
as well as the top-k. Composing that from existing ops (`torch.topk` followed by a `logsumexp`
epilogue) **reads the vocabulary logits three times and materializes two more `[n, V]` temporaries**,
and at a 150k vocabulary that read is the single largest cost in the block. Fusing them makes it one
read and no temporaries. The tile pre-selection is **exact, not approximate** — the argument is in the
function docstring and worth reading before trusting the kernel: if a top-k element's tile were not
among the k tiles with the largest maxima, k other tiles would each hold an element at least as
large, contradicting its rank.

**`lilicorr_greedy_path` — the whole left-to-right commit in one kernel.** The torch form issues
roughly three kernels per slot over `[bs, k]` tensors, so at 15 slots the decode is dozens of
few-microsecond launches and is pure launch overhead rather than arithmetic. Same recurrence, and
`tl.argmax` breaks ties toward the lower index as `Tensor.argmax` does, so the committed path is
identical.

**`lilicorr_sample_path` — that same walk with a sampled commit**, emitting the per-slot proposal the
verify needs to accept it by rejection sampling. A row with `greedy_mask` set takes `tl.argmax` on
the same fp32 node values as the greedy kernel, so one captured graph serves greedy and sampling
batches and the greedy rows walk a bit-identical path.

## Correctness

Verify is unmodified, so **this change cannot alter the distribution of emitted tokens.** Every
drafted token is still checked against the target model exactly as before; a worse drafter would show
up as lower acceptance, never as different output. That is the primary correctness argument, and it
is why the section above measures acceptance rather than task scores.

**Unit tests:** **46 CPU tests** (`test_lilicorr.py`), one worker-stub test in
`test_dflash_logits.py`, and **18 GPU tests** (`test_lilicorr_cuda.py`) pinning all three Triton
kernels against their torch reference implementations on device — vocabulary sizes straddling the
kernel's tile boundary in both directions, bf16 logits as production uses, the narrow-vocabulary
fallback, and the greedy commit at k = 1…16 including tie-breaking. Verified on an H100: 75/75 pass
across the three files. The registry validates — `validate_all_suites()` is clean over 2,487
registered tests — and every pinned pre-commit hook passes over the PR range.

**E2E:** `test/registered/e2e/speculative/test_dflash_lilicorr.py` serves the head through
`--speculative-algorithm DFLASH` with only the draft path changed, and asserts GSM8K accuracy plus
two acceptance floors. It is registered `disabled=` because no drafter is published yet, but it has
been run against one on an H100: `1 passed in 177.19s`, GSM8K 0.950, accept length 5.0392 against a
head-free DFLASH control reading 4.1694 on the same eval.

## Checklist

* Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit — every pinned hook passes over the PR range
* Add unit tests according to Run and add unit tests — 46 CPU tests (`register_cpu_ci`), 18 GPU kernel-parity tests (`register_cuda_ci`), and an E2E server test on the DFlash fixture (`register_cuda_ci`, `disabled=` pending a published drafter)
* Update documentation according to Write documentations — a subsection under "DFlash Decoding"
* Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — see **Performance**
* Follow the SGLang code style guidance

## Design notes

The choices most likely to prompt a question, each also commented at the site.

1. **The head geometry is parsed in `srt/speculative/lilicorr_utils.py`, not as a field on
`DFlashDraftConfig`.** The shared DFLASH config therefore carries no knowledge of this head, at the
cost of one extra `dflash_config` read at model build, and `dflash_utils.py` stays at **zero**
changes.
2. **The lattice attention bias is materialized `[batch*heads, S, S]` rather than broadcast.** The
broadcast form is mathematically identical and saves a copy, but a stride-0 mask measured
**−1.75pp**. Please measure before changing it back.
3. **`F.rms_norm` rather than `sglang.srt.layers.layernorm.RMSNorm`, and a hand-rolled attention**
**module carrying `nn.MultiheadAttention`'s parameter layout.** Same math and the same state\_dict
keys in both cases. The custom-op norm is not capturable here, and the module's Python control flow
and `need_weights` bookkeeping are what make it uncapturable.
4. **The weight loader raises in both directions** — missing head tensors _and_ surplus ones — and
`candidate_topk` must be a power of two, refused at config parse. The surplus direction is live,
not hypothetical: one projection is an `Identity` when the head is as wide as the draft, so a
config omitting the head width would otherwise silently drop it and serve a different architecture
than the one trained. The power-of-two constraint comes from the tiled top-k holding its selected
tiles in a single Triton lane group; supporting other widths would mean serving the head on the
slow reference path, so it is refused at load instead of silently deoptimized.
5. **The convolution coverage check is separate from the head coverage check**, because the two look
at different namespaces: the convolution tensors are backbone parameters named
`layers.*.{attention,mlp}_conv.*`, none of which is under `lilicorr.`, so the head check cannot
see them. See "Convolutional drafters" above for why a missing check is dangerous rather than
merely untidy.
6. **The anchor is worker-owned rather than carried on `DFlashDraftInputV2`.** Carrying it there so
that filter and merge keep it aligned with the batch is the tidier design, but it measured
**−4.67% acceptance** at concurrency 32, and the drift it prevents is not detectable: reordering
cannot happen at concurrency 1 and happens constantly at 32, where acceptance reads 7.5573 and
7.5669. The measurement is recorded at the site in `set_anchor`.

## Known gaps

* **Checkpoints are not yet published.** The docs example carries a placeholder path. The companion
ModelOpt PR linked at the top adds the training and checkpoint export, including the optional
convolutions.
* **`tp>1` serves the head eagerly.** Folding it needs the candidate top-k's packed all-gather
inside the draft graph.

pull_requests.title: [Speculative Decoding] Add native UNO serving support
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

Add native SGLang serving support for UNO, a diffusion-augmented LLM. UNO uses two model pathways:

- The `diffusion pathway` combines the autoregressive (AR) weights with diffusion weights implemented as LoRA adapters.
- The `AR pathway` uses only the base AR weights.

The diffusion pathway drafts a block of tokens in parallel, and the AR pathway verifies those proposals against the base model's autoregressive distribution.

UNO is **lossless** like speculative decoding; however, it does not employ a separate draft model.

Each decoding cycle performs two target-model forward passes:

1. A diffusion-pathway forward pass that produces the first output token and a block of draft proposals.
2. An AR-pathway forward pass that verifies the proposals.

The integration supports two UNO sampling modes. The diffusion pathway constructs marginal distributions for a block of `B` tokens:

1. `Linear sampler:` Samples each token independently from its marginal distribution. This mode is designed to maximize system throughput and uses `B` as its primary hyperparameter.
2. `Tree sampler:` Considers `V` candidate sequences by selecting the top `K` candidates from each marginal distribution. Its hyperparameters are `(B, K, V)`.

## Modifications

- Register `UNO` as a native speculative-decoding algorithm with
  `--uno-lora-path`.
- Validate UNO's CUDA, FA3, parallelism, LoRA, and tree configuration
  constraints at startup.
- Reuse SGLang's existing multi-LoRA manager, adapter representation, layer
  wrappers, and stacked A/B weight buffers. Add an optimized single-adapter
  cuBLAS execution backend that overlaps LoRA-A computation with the base
  GEMMs.
- Apply the UNO LoRA to all but the first row of each draft forward. Use the
  base model alone for target verification.
- Implement sparse and dense proposal and rejection sampling for linear UNO.
- Implement tree UNO sampling and reuse SGLang's existing EAGLE
  tree-verification path.
- Use sparse target sampling for tree verification when eligible; otherwise
  use EAGLE's dense sampling path.
- Add an UNO-only fused kernel for tree-suffix attention and LSE merge, with
  SGLang's existing FlashAttention and state-merge path as fallback.
- Reserve and page-align KV space for UNO's two-pass decode, and extend
  scheduler bookkeeping for its `B + 1` output layout.
- Integrate UNO's carried decode state with SGLang's overlap scheduler.
- Add CUDA-graph support:
  - Linear mode captures separate graph variants for the `B`-wide LoRA draft
    and base-only verification passes.
  - Tree mode uses separate graph runners for the `B`-wide LoRA draft pass and
    `V`-node EAGLE cascade-attention verification pass.
- Add registered CPU dispatch and sampling tests, a CUDA kernel and CUDA-graph
  correctness test for the fused suffix merge, and an end-to-end CUDA-graph
  smoke test using a trained UNO adapter.


## Changes to shared SGLang infrastructure

UNO is implemented primarily in UNO-specific modules. The following extensions
touch shared runtime interfaces but are opt-in or preserve existing defaults:

- LoRA interfaces gain optional support for overlapped LoRA-A execution,
  explicit token-row routing, and skipping inactive internal adapters. Only
  the UNO backend enables these capabilities.
- The shared FlashAttention backend uses the fused suffix-attention merge only
  for eligible UNO tree verification. All other cases retain the existing
  cascade-attention path.
- EAGLE verification accepts optional UNO sampling metadata to select sparse
  target sampling; calls without it retain the existing sampling behavior.
- `GenerationBatchResult` gains optional output-stride and non-draft-token-count
  fields. Scheduler bookkeeping uses them to slice UNO's `B + 1` output rows
  and count accepted proposals; existing algorithms retain their previous
  defaults.
- Speculative allocation sizing uses an UNO-specific branch to reserve the
  additional KV position required by its two-pass decode.
- Model-runner and speculative-registry hooks select the UNO worker and
  CUDA-graph runner only when `--speculative-algorithm UNO` is active.


## Validation

### H200 unit and CUDA smoke validation

The CPU regression tests and the registered H200 CUDA smoke test passed. The
smoke test captured and replayed both linear and tree CUDA-graph paths using
three fixed GSM8K prompts with 128 generated tokens per prompt.

| Mode | B | K | V | TPF |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Linear | 8 | 1 | 8 | 2.462 |
| Tree | 8 | 16 | 8 | 2.783 |

TPF is useful output tokens divided by both target-model forwards per UNO
cycle: `tokens / (2 * spec_verify_ct)`. Tree TPF exceeded linear TPF.

### H200 math evaluation

The runs used `Qwen/Qwen3-8B` in BF16 on one NVIDIA H200 with FA3, a 40,960-token context, and the published [UNO Qwen3-8B adapter](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) for UNO modes. All modes used temperature 1, top-k 50, top-p 0.95, random seed 42, and up to 32,768 output tokens. GSM8K and MATH500 used one sample per problem; AIME25 used 10 samples per problem (300 completions). Each dataset was run separately so it has an independent throughput measurement.

| Mode          | Dataset | Requests | Accuracy |   TPF |   tok/s | tok/s/request |
| ------------- | ------- | -------: | -------: | ----: | ------: | ------------: |
| AR            | GSM8K   |       64 |   96.10% | 1.000 | 6095.61 |         95.24 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | GSM8K   |       64 |   96.00% | 2.590 | 7197.80 |        112.47 |
| AR            | MATH500 |       64 |   96.00% | 1.000 | 3148.58 |         49.20 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | MATH500 |       64 |   95.60% | 2.720 | 5534.55 |         86.48 |
| AR            | AIME25  |       64 |   69.70% | 1.000 | 1894.82 |         29.61 |
| Linear 8/1/8  | AIME25  |       64 |   68.00% | 2.730 | 3841.41 |         60.02 |
| AR            | GSM8K   |        1 |   95.90% | 1.000 |  190.09 |        190.09 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | GSM8K   |        1 |   96.00% | 3.130 |  470.47 |        470.47 |
| AR            | MATH500 |        1 |   96.00% | 1.000 |  183.12 |        183.12 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | MATH500 |        1 |   96.80% | 3.450 |  508.56 |        508.56 |
| AR            | AIME25  |        1 |   68.00% | 1.000 |  178.32 |        178.32 |
| Tree 16/32/32 | AIME25  |        1 |   67.30% | 3.430 |  488.67 |        488.67 |

For UNO modes, the three numbers are `B/K/V`: draft width, top-k candidates kept per position, 
and verification width. Thus, `Linear 8/1/8` uses an
8-token draft width, one candidate per position, and an 8-token verification
width. `tok/s/request` is aggregate throughput divided by the number of
concurrent requests.

### Reproduction

The table was generated with `benchmark/uno/run_math_eval.py`, which
instantiates `sglang.Engine` in-process and excludes engine startup from the
timed interval. Exact commands for reproducing every row are provided in
`benchmark/uno/README.md`.

The equivalent server launch commands for the two UNO configurations are:

```bash
export MODEL_PATH=Qwen/Qwen3-8B
export UNO_LORA_PATH=s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B

# Linear UNO: B/K/V = 8/1/8, 64 concurrent requests
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --context-length 40960 \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --speculative-algorithm UNO \
  --uno-lora-path "$UNO_LORA_PATH" \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 8

# Tree UNO: B/K/V = 16/32/32, one concurrent request
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --attention-backend fa3 \
  --context-length 40960 \
  --max-running-requests 1 \
  --random-seed 42 \
  --speculative-algorithm UNO \
  --uno-lora-path "$UNO_LORA_PATH" \
  --speculative-num-steps 15 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 32 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 32
```


### Test coverage

Added regression coverage for:

- Invalid tree dimensions exceeding the current EAGLE parent-list
  representation.
- Clearing stale internal LoRA metadata before base-only verification.
- Sparse tree target-sampling dispatch and compact-support sampling.
- UNO-only fused suffix-attention dispatch with fallback for unsupported
  attention features and layouts.
- Numerical correctness and CUDA-graph replay of the fused suffix-attention
  merge kernel.
- Linear and tree CUDA-graph capture, replay, generation, and nontrivial
  acceptance.

Current test files:

- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_uno_tree_config.py`
- `test/registered/unit/lora/test_uno_inactive_lora_batch.py`
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_uno_tree_sparse_sampling.py`
- `test/registered/unit/spec/test_suffix_attention_merge_dispatch.py`
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_suffix_attention_merge.py`
- `test/registered/spec/uno/test_uno.py`

## Checklist
- [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance.
- [x] Add unit tests for the new dispatch, sampling, kernel, and end-to-end
  paths.
- [x] Use the published [s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B](https://huggingface.co/s-sahoo/uno-qwen3-8B) adapter.

pull_requests.title: [Speculative] DFlash tree drafting: host-side tree-construction core (#29524)
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

This is the first step toward **JetSpec speculative decoding** (#29524). SGLang's **DFlash** drafts a **linear chain** — one candidate token per draft depth, scored independently of which branch it sits on. JetSpec (Hao AI Lab, [arXiv 2606.18394](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18394)) keeps DFlash's single draft-head forward pass but proposes a **token tree** and verifies the whole tree in one target pass under a tree-causal mask.

The core problem with the chain: **it cannot use a larger draft budget productively.** Once you draft more tokens linearly, acceptance saturates, because a single mispredicted token truncates the whole proposal. A tree spends the same budget on *branches*, so more of it survives verification. Concretely, from the paper (Qwen3-8B, temperature 0):

| Drafting | Accept length τ @ budget 256 (MATH-500) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|
| DFlash chain | saturates ~budget 32 (τ≈6.9), no gain beyond | — |
| EAGLE-3 tree (depth 8, budget 64) | τ≈4.13 | 2.36× |
| **JetSpec tree** | **τ≈10.76** | **9.64×** |

(JetSpec also reports ~1000 TPS on a single B200 and 9.45× on MoE Qwen3-30B-A3B.) The win is structural: same one-pass draft head, but branch scores are conditioned on ancestors and verified as a tree.

This is a large, GPU-bound feature (verify-loop integration, CUDA-graph capture, multiple attention backends, kernels, perf). **This PR lands only the GPU-independent host-side core + plumbing, fully CPU-unit-tested**, so the verify-loop integration can be built on a tested foundation. Tree mode is guarded off at startup; the chain path is byte-for-byte unchanged.

I want to be transparent up front: **I don't currently have GPU access**, so I deliberately stopped at the GPU boundary rather than ship untested kernel/worker code (see Accuracy Tests / Speed Tests). I'd welcome collaboration on the verify-loop wiring and validation — @vincentzed.

## Background — how the tree is built (1 minute)

Per request, the draft head's one forward pass gives per-depth logits. From these we take **top-W tokens + log-probs per depth** (`(depth, W)`), pulled to host. The tree is then built **entirely on CPU**:

- **`opt_prefix`** (paper Algorithm 1): a best-first max-heap keyed by accumulated branch log-prob `Σ log q(y_u | x, h, ancestors)`. Each pop emits one node and pushes its next sibling (same parent, next rank) and first child (next depth, rank 0) — enumerating exactly the top-B highest-probability root→node prefixes without expanding the exponential space.
- **`depth_first`** (default): lays down the greedy top-1 chain (the "spine") first, then adds side branches by accumulated log-prob. Because the spine is always present, **tree acceptance ≥ chain acceptance** by construction — a safe no-regression floor.

The tree is then encoded for verification: a **tree-causal "allow" mask** where each node attends only to the prefix + its ancestors (not siblings/cousins), and SGLang's existing **`retrieve_next_token`/`retrieve_next_sibling`** left-child/right-sibling pointers that the tree-general verify kernels already walk. Acceptance is greedy: a child is accepted iff its token equals the target's argmax at its parent; the longest fully-accepted root→leaf path wins.

This is a faithful port of the reference vLLM integration ([`Jet-Flow/vllm-jetspec`](https://github.com/Jet-Flow/vllm-jetspec)), adapted to SGLang's DFlash/EAGLE conventions.

## Modifications

**New `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_tree.py`** — pure-Python/torch, no sglang-internal imports, no GPU:
- `build_tree_opt_prefix`, `build_tree_depth_first`, and a `build_tree` dispatcher (caps fan-out to `tree_width`).
- `tree_to_verify_buffers` — tree → SGLang verify buffers (`retrieve_next_token`/`retrieve_next_sibling` with the `-1` sentinel, `positions`, padded to budget).
- `build_tree_custom_mask` / `build_ancestor_mask` — tree-causal mask in the existing flattened `Σkv·N + N²·bs` layout.
- `compute_tree_budget`, `DFlashDraftTree` (`msgspec.Struct`), and `verify_tree_greedy_cpu` (CPU reference of greedy tree acceptance — test oracle + eager fallback).

**Plumbing:**
- `server_args.py` — `--speculative-dflash-tree-{width,budget,construction}` (documented as guarded/inert until the verify-loop integration lands).
- `arg_groups/speculative_hook.py` — `_handle_dflash_tree` rejects `--speculative-dflash-tree-width > 1` at startup with a clear message, so the flag can't trigger an unimplemented path. `width <= 1` (chain) is unaffected.
- `dflash_info.py` — `DFlashVerifyInput.from_tree` (populates the existing `topk`/`custom_mask` fields) and `build_dflash_tree_verify_input` (draft top-W output → tree-mode verify input): the seam the worker integration will call.
- `test/registered/spec/dflash/test_dflash_tree.py` — CPU unit + integration suite (`register_cpu_ci`, `base-a-test-cpu`).

**Key design decisions:**
1. **Reuse the tree-general verify kernels** (`verify_tree_greedy` / `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only`), **not** `build_tree_kernel_efficient` — a best-first tree is general and doesn't fit EAGLE's per-step beam `parent_list` format, whereas the verify kernels consume our hand-built `retrieve_*` + `custom_mask` directly. **No new kernels.**
2. **`tree_width == 1` is byte-identical to the current chain buffers** (`retrieve_next_token = t→t+1`, last `-1`; `retrieve_next_sibling` all `-1`) — asserted in a test against the actual `_get_or_create_chain_verify_buffers`. Existing DFlash users are unaffected.
3. **The DFlash worker decode loop is intentionally untouched** (zero risk to the chain path); tree mode is wired through the new bridge in a follow-up.

**Deferred (follow-up, GPU-bound):** wiring the tree path into `dflash_worker_v2`'s verify loop — CUDA-graph capture for a *variable-size* tree, and the **non-contiguous accepted-path KV commit** (the chain path assumes a contiguous accepted prefix); plus `trtllm_mha`/`flashinfer` tree-verify, MoE/hybrid recurrent-tree commit, SM90/SM100, rejection-sampling tree, and perf.

## Accuracy Tests

This PR does **not change model outputs**: tree mode is guarded off at startup, and the chain path is byte-identical (asserted). So there is no accuracy delta to report here.

The host-side core is validated by a CPU-only suite (no GPU, no server):
- **Keystone integration test** — a faithful CPU simulation of the CUDA `verify_tree_greedy` traversal (follow `retrieve_next_token` → `retrieve_next_sibling`) is asserted **equal** to an independent parent-based acceptance oracle over **200 random trees × both builders**. This validates that the buffer encoding the GPU kernel will consume matches the tree the host built — the central correctness argument that substitutes for a GPU run.
- **W=1 byte-equivalence** to the legacy chain buffers (via the real `_get_or_create_chain_verify_buffers`).
- Builder invariants (parent < child, depth consistency, budget cap, opt_prefix best-first ordering, depth_first spine guarantee), tree-causal mask semantics + size formula, full edge-case coverage (empty depth, budget 0/1, budget > full-tree, single depth, ties, padding, batch), and the startup-guard + bridge.

The **end-to-end lossless-greedy accuracy test** — tree-spec output token-identical to non-spec decode on `triton`/`fa3` with `JetSpec/jetspec-qwen3-8b` — is the merge gate for the follow-up verify-loop wiring. It requires a GPU (which I don't currently have); the code is structured (bridge + oracle) so it's straightforward to validate once the loop is wired, and I'd appreciate a hand running it.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed impact in this PR — tree mode is guarded off and the chain path is unchanged. Throughput / acceptance-length benchmarking (tree vs chain across budgets; SM90/SM100) is part of the deferred follow-up and requires a GPU; not included here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit (black + isort + ruff lint; verified clean).
- [x] Add unit tests (CPU unit + integration suite under `test/registered/spec/dflash/`).
- [ ] Update documentation — N/A for this PR (no user-facing feature yet; flags documented in `--help` and marked inert/guarded).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results — deferred: tree mode isn't runnable yet (guarded) and I have no GPU; this is the follow-up's merge gate (see above).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## References

- Issue: #29524 · Paper: [arXiv 2606.18394](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18394) · Blog: https://haoailab.com/blogs/parallel-tree-decoding
- Reference integration: [`Jet-Flow/vllm-jetspec`](https://github.com/Jet-Flow/vllm-jetspec) · Draft heads: https://huggingface.co/JetSpec

Resolves part of #29524.

pull_requests.title: [Sepc]Dflash2 tree drafting
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

This PR extends DFLASH from single-path drafting to selector-based beam-tree drafting.
The selector already computes top-K candidates and transition scores for every draft
position; tree drafting retains multiple candidates instead of collapsing them to one
path.

The target verifies the tree with an ancestor mask, then the accepted path is compacted
back into the existing chain-shaped acceptance and KV-cache bookkeeping. A node budget
limits verification cost independently from the per-depth beam width. Nodes are selected
by cumulative selector log-probability while preserving ancestor closure. This is a
serving heuristic, not a claim that selector scores exactly optimize target acceptance.

Tree verification currently supports greedy decoding only. The default `W=1` chain path
and chain sampling behavior remain unchanged unless tree verification is explicitly
enabled.

## Configuration

| name | meaning | value in the runs below |
|---|---|---|
| `block_size` | draft forward positions, anchor included | 8 |
| `gamma = block_size - 1` | maximum tree depth | 7 |
| `W` (`--speculative-dflash-tree-width`) | beam width per draft depth | 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 |
| `max_num_nodes` (`SGLANG_DFLASH_MAX_NUM_NODES`) | node budget; `0` means unbounded | 0 / 12 / 15 / 30 / 60 |
| `N` (`speculative_num_draft_tokens`) | nodes submitted to verify | `full_width` when cap is 0, otherwise `min(full_width, max_num_nodes)` |
| `K` (`selector_top_k`) | selector candidates per position | 16 |

Configuration constraints:

- `W=1` keeps the existing chain path by default.
- `W>1` requires `W <= K`, `page_size=1`, and a tree-capable target attention backend (`flashinfer`, `triton`, or `fa3`).
- Tree verification supports greedy decoding only. Sampling requests are rejected while tree verification is active; chain sampling remains supported.
- `SGLANG_DFLASH_MAX_NUM_NODES` must be `0` or at least `block_size`. A positive cap at or above `full_width` is a no-op.
- `SGLANG_DFLASH_FORCE_TREE_VERIFY` is a debug-only switch for routing `W=1` through the tree path.

## Implementation

- **Width plumbing**: draft, verify, and beam widths use independent values, with buffers and CUDA-graph shapes sized from the appropriate width.
- **Beam walk**: builds a BFS-ordered beam over the selector lattice and retains the greedy spine.
- **Tree verification**: derives ancestor masks, positions, and retrieve links, then compacts the accepted path back to chain-shaped scheduler and KV-cache state.
- **CUDA graph support**: writes the flat verify mask on device into the backend-owned buffer, removing the per-step blocking host copy.
- **Node pruning**: ranks cumulative scores with a Triton kernel and has an independent torch reference implementation.

## Correctness

**Width-one equivalence.** Compared with the pre-PR chain path using identical flags and
concurrency 1: 768 generated tokens were identical, per-request accept lengths matched,
and `max|delta logprob| = 0.0`. The on-device mask rewrite was also byte-identical on
`W=4`, forced tree verification at `W=1`, and the chain path.

The registered tests cover beam construction, ancestor closure, pruned-tree metadata,
tree acceptance and compaction, width/node-budget resolution, sampling admission, mask
writing, pruning tie behavior, bounds, non-finite cumulative scores, and Triton-vs-torch
reference agreement.

**Known correctness gap.** `W>1` has not yet been validated against an autoregressive
baseline. Some W>1 runs differ from the W=1 chain in log probabilities by up to roughly
`7e-2`; this may be caused by reduction-order changes from the wider verify batch, but it
has not been formally attributed. W>1 AR output parity should be checked before merge.

## Performance

Measured on 1x NVIDIA GB200 (device reports `CF-NG-GBZZ2-O-L`, compute capability 10.0,
188729 MiB), with Qwen3.8-27B + DFlash2 draft (GDN + GQA target), `block_size=8`,
decode CUDA graph enabled, bs=1, greedy, ShareGPT prompts (32 x 512 output tokens),
seed 42.

Environment: Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA runtime 13.0, CUDA toolkit
13.2, NVIDIA driver 580.159.03, SGLang commit `7b13998137`.

| W | `max_num_nodes` | N | accept len | mean TPOT | output tok/s |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 (chain path) | - | 8 | 3.67 | 3.73 ms | 255.9 |
| 8 | 12 | 12 | 4.31 | **3.52 ms** | **269.6** |
| 2 | 15 | 15 | 4.28 | 3.64 ms | 261.6 |
| 4 | 15 | 15 | 4.38 | 3.56 ms | 267.1 |
| 8 | 15 | 15 | 4.42 | **3.52 ms** | 269.5 |
| 16 | 15 | 15 | 4.42 | 3.53 ms | 268.6 |
| 4 | 30 | 29 | 4.55 | 3.89 ms | 244.6 |
| 8 | 30 | 30 | 4.59 | 3.89 ms | 245.3 |
| 16 | 30 | 30 | 4.63 | 3.87 ms | 246.4 |
| 8 | 60 | 57 | 4.88 | 4.83 ms | 199.0 |
| 16 | 60 | 60 | 4.92 | 4.92 ms | 195.4 |
| 16 | 0 (unbounded) | 113 | 5.24 | 6.54 ms | 147.8 |

The best measured point is `W=8`, `max_num_nodes=15`: `-5.6%` TPOT and `+5.3%`
output tok/s versus the chain. Larger trees improve accept length but are slower; at
the same `N=15`, `W=8/16` outperform `W=2` on accept length (4.42 vs. 4.28).

For a 100-step torch profile at `W=16`, `N=15`, bs=4, and 8192-token contexts, the
device-side mask rewrite reduced inter-kernel gaps from 5.5 to 0 per step, removed the
1.03 blocking `Device -> Pageable` copies per step, and reduced GPU idle from 15.1% to
4.0%.

## Limitations

- W>1 autoregressive output parity has not been measured yet.
- Tree verification is greedy-only and currently requires the listed attention backends and `page_size=1`.
- Accept length is workload-dependent; the benchmark rows are not general model-quality claims.
- Dense convolution-window and full tree-mask memory costs are not included in the reported accounting.
- NPU and AMX W>1 paths have not been exercised.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code according to [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update repository documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The configuration and limitations are documented above, but the formal docs pages still need the new flags.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

pull_requests.title: [Speculative] Add RACER: reuse target logits for training-free tree drafting
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

This PR adds **RACER**, a training-free speculative decoding method that reuses **target verification logits as an additional draft source**.

- Paper: [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.998)
- Code: [github.com/hkr04/RACER](https://github.com/hkr04/RACER)

Existing NGRAM speculation retrieves continuations from token history. Like NGRAM, RACER retrieves continuations from token history, but uses an Aho-Corasick automaton for retrieval and augments it with top-k alternatives already produced during `TARGET_VERIFY`.

**No draft model, no training, no draft KV cache, and no extra target forward pass for decode-time logits.**

```text
Token history ──→ AC retrieval ──────┐
                                     ├──→ draft tree
Past target logits → Logits Tree ────┘
```

The main goal of this PR is to demonstrate that **verification logits are useful reusable speculative-decoding state**, and that tree drafts can be assembled from multiple inexpensive sources.

## Modifications

- Add RACER as a training-free speculative algorithm.
- Reuse SGLang's existing irregular-tree `TARGET_VERIFY` path.
- Save target top-k logits from verified nodes into a per-request Logits Tree.
- Let history retrieval take priority; logits only fill remaining unique draft slots.
- Warm up both prompt history and prompt logits.
- Add unit tests for RACER draft generation / unique-budget behavior.

## Performance

Official SPEED-Bench setup:

`mixed / 1K ISL / 512 OSL / 512 prompts / concurrency=1 / BF16 / TP=1`

### Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct / RTX 3090

| Method    |  K |   Accept | Output tok/s |   Speedup |
| --------- | -: | -------: | -----------: | --------: |
| Vanilla   |  — |        — |        49.71 |     1.00× |
| NGRAM | 32 |     2.05 |        90.41 |     1.82× |
| RACER     | 32 | **2.53** |    **95.24** | **1.92×** |
| NGRAM | 64 |     2.15 |        90.75 |     1.83× |
| RACER     | 64 | **2.90** |   **102.34** | **2.06×** |

### Qwen3.8-27B / A800 80GB

| Method    |  K |   Accept | Output tok/s |   Speedup |
| --------- | -: | -------: | -----------: | --------: |
| Vanilla   |  — |        — |        27.00 |     1.00× |
| NGRAM | 16 |     1.80 |        40.34 |     1.49× |
| RACER     | 16 | **2.06** |    **42.30** | **1.57×** |
| NGRAM | 32 |     1.89 |        37.74 |     1.40× |
| RACER     | 32 | **2.50** |    **45.30** | **1.68×** |

At K32, target verification already costs **1.29× T(1)**, but RACER still improves throughput by **20.0% over same-K NGRAM**. This suggests the gain is not limited to hardware where wide verification is nearly free.

### ShareGPT sanity check

We also tested raw ShareGPT prompts through SGLang's `/generate` endpoint (`K=32`, trie depth 10):

> Ran with the official SGLang serving benchmark: `python -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name sharegpt` (official ShareGPT loader).

| Model | Vanilla | NGRAM | RACER |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen2.5-7B / 3090 | 49.24 | 71.38 (**1.45×**) | **95.00 (1.93×)** |
| Qwen3.8-27B / A800 | 27.70 | 28.15 (**1.02×**) | **41.03 (1.48×)** |

This is not a chat-serving benchmark, but it highlights a useful difference between the draft sources: **history-only NGRAM becomes much less effective when reusable context patterns are sparse, while RACER can still obtain candidates from target logits**.

## Accuracy

Official SGLang GSM8K evaluation, Qwen3.8-27B / A800 TP1:

`200 examples / temperature=0 / thinking disabled`

| Method  |     K |  Accuracy |   Accept | Eval tok/s |
| ------- | ----: | --------: | -------: | ---------: |
| Vanilla |     — | **96.5%** |        — |       27.7 |
| NGRAM   |    16 | **96.5%** |     1.92 |       42.3 |
| NGRAM   |    32 | **96.5%** |     2.11 |       40.6 |
| RACER   |    16 | **96.5%** |     2.09 |       41.8 |
| RACER   |    32 | **96.5%** | **2.54** |   **43.9** |
| RACER   |    48 |     97.0% |     2.78 |       40.3 |
| MTP     | s3/K4 | **96.5%** |     3.64 |       75.7 |

RACER K16/K32 preserves the Vanilla **96.5% GSM8K accuracy**.

MTP is shown only as a model-specific reference: it is substantially faster when MTP weights are available, while RACER targets the **model-agnostic, training-free** setting.

## Relation to NGRAM

RACER is closely related to **NGRAM + logits-assisted expansion**. In our experiments, adding a `min_match_depth` constraint to NGRAM and then filling the remaining tree budget with a Logits Tree produces behavior close to RACER, which may help isolate the value of target-logit reuse from RACER-specific retrieval details. We plan to submit this simpler `NGRAM_LOGITS` variant separately.

## Current limitations

- Overlap scheduling is not yet supported.
-  Performance evaluation currently focuses on **TP=1**. TP>1 is supported, but the speculative speedup can be largely offset by additional verification and communication overhead.
- RACER is ultimately **bounded by target verification cost**. Unlike trained drafters such as MTP/DFlash, RACER does not directly improve the verifier/drafter quality through training; in our training-free setting, **accept length eventually grows more slowly than verification cost as K increases**, limiting the achievable end-to-end speedup.

This PR is primarily intended to expose and evaluate the **target-logit reuse / multi-source drafting** idea; further runtime optimization can be handled independently.

pull_requests.body:
# [Feat] speculative: Add native UBTree decoding for Ling3

## Motivation

This PR provides native SGLang inference support for the released UBTree draft checkpoints:

- [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree), paired with [Ling-3.0-tiny](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny).
- [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree), paired with [Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash).

UBTree combines a parallel DFlash proposer with a learned bigram selector to build a proposal tree. The target verifies the tree in one forward pass and commits the accepted continuation. The draft checkpoints are used alongside their matching target models and share the target's token embeddings and LM head.

For KDA linear attention, saving a complete recurrent state for every proposal node adds memory traffic and temporary storage. This PR uses a shared pre-tree state and per-node factors, then folds only the accepted path into persistent state. It also includes checkpoint loading, tree construction, and fixed-width CUDA Graph execution in SGLang.

## Modifications

- Native UBTree serving for Ling3 Tiny and Flash: built-in algorithm registration, draft-checkpoint loading, selector caches, tensor-parallel vocabulary top-k, and proposal-tree construction.
- Factorized Triton KDA tree verification using a shared pre-tree recurrent state and root-to-node factors.
- Fused causal convolution and tree transformation to prepare factor-generation inputs with fewer intermediate launches and tensor transfers.
- Accepted-path KDA/convolution-state and target/draft-KV commit through a shared verification epilogue for eager execution and CUDA Graph replay.
- Fixed-width BS=1 full decode CUDA Graph execution covering draft proposals, target verification, and accepted-path commit.
- FA3 tree-verification metadata with a `QLEN_ONLY` visibility mask.
- NVIDIA L20X Triton 3.7.1 MoE forward and down-projection tuning configurations for Ling expert shapes.
- Component, selector, tree-topology, kernel, backend, and CUDA Graph replay regression tests.

## Supported Scope

| Item | Supported configuration |
|---|---|
| Target models | Ling-3.0-tiny and Ling-3.0-flash (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`) |
| Released draft checkpoints | [Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree) and [Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree), both B16 |
| Ling3 Tiny verification | 49 nodes; TP1 startup validated |
| Ling3 Flash verification | 32 nodes; TP4 startup validated |
| Ling3 Flash draft blocks | 8 and 16 exercised during development; the linked release is B16 |
| Scheduling | One active request, greedy decoding, DP=1, PP=1 |
| Linear attention backend | Triton KDA |
| Full attention backend | FA3 for both target and draft, page size 1 |
| CUDA Graph | Fixed-width full decode, BS=1; prefill graphs and graph padding disabled |

**B16 is the draft block size, not the verification-tree width.** Select the runtime verification width with `--speculative-num-draft-tokens`; the current native path supports 32 or 49 nodes within the checkpoint's tree budget.

## Integration Boundary

This PR includes the SGLang runtime support needed to serve the two linked UBTree releases:

- draft-checkpoint loading and selector-cache materialization;
- proposal-node selection and tree construction;
- factorized KDA verification and recurrent-state management;
- accepted-path state and KV commit;
- FA3 tree metadata and CUDA Graph capture/replay.

Model training, checkpoint export, and model weights remain outside SGLang. The native serving path does not require an external Ling-Spec UBTree runtime plugin.

UBTree dispatch uses the built-in algorithm and explicit tree metadata. Backend regression tests cover the existing snapshot path alongside the new tree path.

Launch with `--speculative-algorithm UBTREE` and the matching `--speculative-draft-model-path`. The [Tiny model card](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree#serving-with-sglang) and [Flash model card](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree#serving-with-sglang) provide full launch commands using the PR's [`asahi/ubtree` branch](https://github.com/AsaHIXx/sglang/tree/asahi/ubtree).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Test protocol

The table below retains the previously reported PR measurements. Their benchmark revision was not specified in the original description.

| Item | Setting |
|---|---|
| Datasets | GSM8K, MATH-500, AIME25, HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench |
| Model | Ling3 Flash |
| Batch size | 1 |

The released [Tiny](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny-UBTree#benchmark-results) and [Flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-UBTree#benchmark-results) model cards contain reproduce server commands.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

<!-- PR title: [Type] scope: title, or [Type] [Hardware] scope: title.
Type: Feat, Fix, Refactor, Perf, Doc, Test, CI, or Chore.
Scope: any module or model name (no fixed list or letter-case restriction), e.g. attention, qwen3, or flash-attn.

Title: no letter-case restriction.
Reverts: use GitHub's default title, Revert "original title".
Examples: [Fix] attention: Fix KV cache indexing; [Perf] [AMD] flash-attn: Optimize decode performance. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The unquantized DFLASH draft `fc` projects the concatenated target hidden taps to the draft hidden size. It is replicated on every TP rank, so every rank reads the whole weight once per decode cycle: K = num_context_features x hidden, N = hidden, 2 x K x N bytes of bf16.

## Modifications
Opt-in via `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_SPLIT_FC=1` (default off; nothing changes when it is off):

- With the flag on, `DFlashDraftModel.project_target_hidden` computes `fc` with the existing column-parallel GEMM + multicast all-gather helper `gemm_ag` (`layers/communication/muse_spark_gemm_ag.py`):
  - each rank runs the bf16 GEMM dispatch on its `N / TP` row block of the replicated weight, reading 1 / TP of the bytes;
  - one multicast all-gather through `CustomAllReduceV2` then assembles the full output.
- `gemm_ag` needs the same input on every rank of the TP group, so the flag is ignored under attention DP and prefill context parallel, where ranks of the draft's TP group can hold different tokens. Layernorm sequence parallelism is safe: `validate_layernorm_sp` rejects it with speculative decoding unless the target all-gathers the aux hidden states (`sp_exit_gather`) before the draft reads them, so the draft `fc` input is replicated.
- It falls back to `self.fc` whenever `gemm_ag_supported()` rejects the call:
  - TP = 1 or no multicast;
  - non-bf16 data;
  - M > 512, or an M x N bf16 output larger than the push workspace;
  - for M > 8, anything other than SM 10.3 at TP4 / TP8 with N = 4096 or 8192.

  The default `CustomAllReduceV2` push workspace on SM100-class GPUs is 4 MB at TP4 and 2 MB at TP8. So on SM 10.3 a draft with N = 8192 takes the new path up to M = 256 (TP4) / 128 (TP8), and N = 4096 up to M = 512 / 256, with no extra reservation. On other GPUs only M <= 8 does.
- The Laguna draft overrides `project_target_hidden` and does not use the flag.

Why the weight stays replicated instead of a column-parallel `fc` with an output gather:
- the loader stays unchanged;
- `ColumnParallelLinear(gather_output=True)` gathers through NCCL. We measured it at 18.5 us per call at TP4 (~20 us across trays at TP8), against 8.5 us for the multicast gather, plus a reshape copy for the last-dim gather.

Why opt-in: the gain beyond M = 8 needs SM 10.3 at TP4 / TP8, and the slice GEMM is not bitwise equal to the replicated GEMM.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Sanity check with the flag on. For reference, the same setup without this flag (main + the tuned draft GEMM PR) measured GSM8K 97.50% and AIME26 pass@1 95.83% ± 3.33%.

| Model | GSM8K (x1, 65K max tokens) | AIME26 pass@1 (30 x 16, 131K) | AIME26 pass@16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Muse Spark Open (NVFP4, TP4, DFLASH) + this PR | 97.80% | 96.25% ± 2.69% (std over 16 runs; SEM 0.67%) | 100% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Muse Spark Open NVFP4, GB300, DFLASH, acceptance length fixed at 4.05. nsys of one replayed 8K-input / 512-output wave per concurrency, flag off -> on, FlashInfer autotune off on both sides. The table shows the exposed time of the changed kernels per decode cycle and its share of the cycle. The changed kernels are the fc GEMM, replaced by a 1/TP slice GEMM plus the multicast all-gather.

| | c=1 | c=2 | c=4 | c=8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 (us/cycle) | -68.3 (**-0.73%**) | -68.2 (**-0.63%**) | -66.5 (**-0.50%**) | -74.8 (**-0.46%**) |
| TP8 (us/cycle) | -76.4 (**-1.01%**) | -77.0 (**-0.91%**) | -79.3 (**-0.81%**) | -85.3 (**-0.71%**) |

At TP4 c=1: fc 102.7 us -> slice GEMM 28.6 us + all-gather 8.5 us. No NCCL all-gather is added.

pull_requests.title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dflash: Top up decode KV pages for the whole batch on allocation steps
pull_requests.body:
## Motivation

`DFlashDraftInputV2.prepare_for_decode` allocates KV pages only for the requests whose committed length plus the 2-block reserve crosses their allocated length. With page size 256 and accept length ~3.5, each request crosses a page about every 73 decode steps. In a DEP32 c5768 nsys profile (~36 running per rank), a rank allocated on ~35% of its steps, and each allocation step cost ~0.78 ms of host time, mostly `get_last_loc` (95 us), paged `alloc_extend` (578 us) and the `req_to_token` assign (56 us).

Under attention DP this sits before the DP agreement. With 32 ranks allocating independently, some rank pays it on nearly every step, and the whole step waits for that rank.

## Modifications

`SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_DECODE_TOPUP_PAGES=K` (default 2; 0 turns it off; capped at 8 pages) changes what happens on a step that must allocate anyway:
- Every request below K pages of headroom is topped up to K pages beyond its page-aligned need, in the same `alloc_for_spec_decode` call.
- The top-up is bounded by the `req_to_token` row width.
- Already-running requests then next need pages about K pages of decode later. A rank's allocations are batched into shared allocation steps instead of one step per request page crossing.
- The top-up is skipped unless the allocator's free tokens cover the paged-extend eviction demand (`needed + top-up + bs x page_size`, the demand `take_extend` passes to `make_room`) plus 3x the top-up. When it is skipped, the step allocates exactly as before. So on the full/SWA token pools the top-up does not trigger a prefix-cache eviction that the step would not have done anyway. (The NPU DSV4 C128 sidecar pool is not part of this check; this path was not run on NPU.)
- The top-up is skipped under HiSparse (with a one-time warning only when the env is set explicitly). HiSparse's spec-decode path always evicts, and it sizes its host pool by `kv_allocated_len`.

Admission becomes slightly more conservative. Decode admission subtracts a per-running-request decode reservation from the free size, and the free size already excludes the topped-up pages. So up to K pages per running request are counted twice. On a PD decode worker the reservation is `--num-reserved-decode-tokens` (512), so at page size 256 and K=2 the worst case doubles it (512 more tokens per running request; 98k tokens at 192 running). This is self-limiting: the guard caps a top-up at a quarter of the free tokens beyond `needed + bs x page_size`, so as free tokens approach the reservation the top-ups shrink and stop, and decode uses up the pages already held.

Behavior change: the top-up is on by default (K=2) for every DFlash-family decode with a page size above 1. K=2 is the only value measured; it holds at most 2 extra pages per running request, and the free-space guard above makes it fall back to exact allocation when memory is tight.

The change is independent of #47676, #47677 and #47678 (the other DSV4.1 decode host-path changes). It was measured stacked on them.

## Accuracy Tests

All runs: GB300, DSV4.1-Flash, K=2, on a 2026-10-30 nightly.

- Consistency check (diagnostic overlay, not part of this PR): on every allocation step, the check verifies that each newly allocated `[cur, nxt)` range of `req_to_token` is nonzero, is not shared with any other request's new range, and that `kv_allocated_len` equals `nxt`. Result: 870 checks, 0 bad.
- GSM8K, 1P1D DEP16 with real DSpark acceptance, same run: 96.82% (control without the top-up, with the other three changes: 96.82%).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DEP32 c5768 (10P1D). This comparison isolates the top-up: both arms have #47676-#47678, and the arm adds `SGLANG_OPT_DFLASH_DECODE_TOPUP_PAGES=2`.

| | without top-up | with top-up |
|---|---|---|
| decode step p50, 32-47 running | 13.9 ms | 13.7 ms |
| steady-window per-GPU throughput (prompt + completion tokens, mean of minutes 8-20, x0.96 both arms) | 660.6k tok/s/GPU | 687.8k tok/s/GPU |
| p90 interactivity | 219.8 tok/s/user | 223.4 tok/s/user |

The throughput gain (+4.1%) comes from a single pair of separate runs, and each run has one dip bin (control at minutes 10-12, arm at minutes 14-16). Run-to-run drift on this shape can reach ~3%, so the throughput delta is not conclusive on its own. The step-time reduction (-0.2 ms p50) is the signal.

9P1D DEP16 bs192 c7480 checks a high-batch, KV-heavy shape. It compares all four host changes against none, so it is not an isolated measurement of the top-up:
- decode step p50 is 0.2-0.26 ms lower in every max-running bucket (33.64 -> 33.38 ms at 192 running);
- throughput is neutral: 1127.2k vs 1127.2k tok/s/GPU at p90 100.0 vs 101.2 tok/s/user;
- KV headroom: full KV usage max 0.55 -> 0.54; SWA usage mean 0.063 -> 0.112 (max 0.16 -> 0.23); 0 retracted requests in both.

At these loads the low-free skip path is not exercised. In the GSM8K run the consistency check also logged the free size: on every allocation step, free tokens were at least 15.8x the skip bound. The GPU runs used the guard before the `bs x page_size` term was added; the term adds 10k tokens at 40 running and 49k at 192.

pull_requests.title: [DCP][Spec] EAGLE/EAGLE3 support for decode context parallelism
pull_requests.body:
Makes **EAGLE / EAGLE3** work with decode context parallelism (`--dcp-size > 1`). Stacked on #21637.

DFlash × DCP already worked (see #33912, `_dflash_draft_cell_size`); it gets one shared fix here, not new support.

**Root cause:** the target KV pool is sharded across DCP ranks, but the draft pool is **replicated**. Draft-side code that reads the DCP topology therefore builds rank-local metadata against a full pool. Every change below follows from that.


## Results

8×B200, K2.5-NVFP4 + EAGLE3 (ns2/topk1/ndt3), `--dcp-comm-backend a2a --dcp-replicate-q-proj`,
jobs 1496709–1496996. Accept length is the correctness gate: the DCP arm must match the off arm,
since a draft chain fed rank-local metadata degenerates after the first token.

| config | off (ms) | DCP=8 (ms) | ratio | AL off → DCP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50K / cc4 | 4.96 | 5.93 | 0.84× | 2.239 → 2.234 |
| 128K / cc16 | 19.58 | 20.44 | 0.96× | 2.160 → 2.150 |
| 128K / cc24 | 37.66 | **26.78** | **1.41×** | 2.172 → 2.163 |
| 256K / cc8 | 20.63 | 22.19 | 0.93× | 1.756 → 1.781 |
| 256K / cc16 | 59.51 | **38.14** | **1.56×** | 1.748 → 1.745 |

GSM8K 0.940–0.960 on every arm. Below the KV-pool edge DCP pays the verify addon for no benefit; past it the off arm loses admission first and DCP wins. Attention FLOPs are conserved under context sharding, so there is no headroom to beat the off arm at shallow overcommit — the ~16% cost at 50K/cc4 is the design point, not a regression.

## Tests

`test_dcp_draft_guard.py`, `test_dcp_draft_pool_bounds.py`, `test_dcp_spec_topk_guard.py` — all three cover failures that are otherwise **silent**: a guard that stops unsharding draft forwards corrupts the chain with no error, an under-budgeted draft pool OOMs at the first large prefill far from its cause, and a mis-scoped topk validator returns wrong tokens rather than raising. The topk tests pin that DSPARK is *not* gated (`is_dflash_family()` would pull it in and reject the shipping Kimi-Linear + DSPARK + DCP path).

Registered DCP/spec suites pass on 8×B200, including main's `test_kimi_linear_dcp4.py`.
